display.purpose: Screen titles and the Battle Plan wordmark.

label.purpose: Buttons, tabs, and compact state labels.

mono.purpose: Relay codes and compact technical values only.

shadows.name: toy-edge
shadows.purpose: Firm structural bottom edge for controls and plates.

shadows.name: toy-edge-pressed
shadows.purpose: Pressed state that visually settles into the play surface.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Button color, border, and press feedback.

motion.name: character-ambient
motion.purpose: One existing character loop or pose supplies each screen's ambient personality.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single next-step action in a decision group.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height:52px; padding:10px 16px 12px; border:3px solid #1B1927; border-bottom-width:6px; border-radius:10px; background:#F2A54A; color:#1B1927; font:700 15px Rubik, sans-serif; transition:background 100ms ease-out, border-color 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#FFBA5C; border-color:#F5ECD8; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { border-width:5px 5px 6px; border-color:#84D3E6; outline:none; } .ds-btn-primary:active { border-bottom-width:3px; padding-top:13px; padding-bottom:9px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A tactile action that does not compete with the primary step.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height:52px; padding:10px 16px 12px; border:3px solid #1B1927; border-bottom-width:6px; border-radius:10px; background:#3A3B52; color:#F5ECD8; font:700 15px Rubik, sans-serif; transition:background 100ms ease-out, border-color 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background:#474862; border-color:#F5ECD8; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { border-width:5px 5px 6px; border-color:#84D3E6; outline:none; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { border-bottom-width:3px; }

components.name: Selected Option
components.description: A chosen mode, opponent, or unit.
components.css: .ds-btn-selected { min-height:52px; padding:10px 16px 12px; border:3px solid #F5ECD8; border-bottom-width:6px; border-radius:10px; background:#55B29D; color:#1B1927; font:700 15px Rubik, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-selected:hover { background:#55B29D; } .ds-btn-selected:focus-visible { border-width:5px 5px 6px; border-color:#84D3E6; background:#459E8B; outline:none; }

components.name: Toy Panel
components.description: An opaque operating surface placed beside or over the world character stage.
components.css: .ds-toy-panel { padding:24px; border:2px solid #1B1927; border-bottom-width:5px; border-radius:14px; background:#2D2E43; color:#F5ECD8; font:400 15px Rubik, sans-serif; } .ds-toy-panel h2 { margin:0 0 8px; font-size:20px; } .ds-toy-panel p { margin:0; color:#BDB6C9; }

components.name: Toy Readout
components.description: A compact opaque plate for phase, timer, match, and objective information.
components.css: .ds-toy-readout { padding:12px 16px; border:2px solid #1B1927; border-bottom-width:5px; border-radius:10px; background:#2D2E43; color:#F5ECD8; font:400 15px Rubik, sans-serif; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: A short state token for fog, objective control, busy, success, or danger.
components.css: .ds-status-chip { min-height:28px; padding:4px 9px; border:2px solid #1B1927; border-radius:6px; background:#3A3B52; color:#F5ECD8; font:700 12px Rubik, sans-serif; }

components.name: Relay Input
components.description: Large code entry with a stable focus border.
components.css: .ds-relay-input { min-height:52px; padding:10px 14px; border:3px solid #575168; border-radius:10px; background:#1B1927; color:#F5ECD8; font:700 20px 'Cascadia Code', monospace; } .ds-relay-input:hover { border-color:#BDB6C9; } .ds-relay-input:focus-visible { border-width:5px; border-color:#84D3E6; outline:none; }

components.name: Plan Path
components.description: One compact route cue per wide screen.
components.css: .ds-plan-path { display:flex; align-items:center; height:22px; } .ds-plan-start,.ds-plan-stop { width:12px; height:12px; background:#F2A54A; border:2px solid #1B1927; } .ds-plan-start { border-radius:50%; } .ds-plan-line { width:74px; height:4px; background:#F2A54A; }

narrative.overview: Battle Plan should feel like opening a well-loved strategy game and finding its pieces already acting out the next match. Rounded low-poly characters, off-axis poses, and occasional goofy animation supply the charm. The interface behaves like the printed play surface around them: solid, concise, and easy to operate.
keyCharacteristics: Real in-world character models behind reserved transparent UI regions.
Chunky, tactile controls with firm outlines and short offset depth.
Mixed-case, plain-language labels with very little supporting copy.
Warm orange decisions, teal confirmation, and tomato error states.
One animated character moment per screen, never motion everywhere.

rules.name: The Character Color Rule
rules.body: Saturated colors identify a decision or state. They do not decorate empty space.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: If a label already names the action, do not add a sentence that repeats it.

rules.name: The One Stage Rule
rules.body: Each screen has one depth-bearing character stage. Nested floating panels do not compete with it.

dos: Do use the project’s actual rounded models and existing humorous poses.
Do reserve opaque reading surfaces around every label, input, and status message.
Do pair color with an icon, outline, check, count, or text state.
Do let Pogo Rider carry the strongest recurring motion.
donts: Don't use realistic soldiers, photographic portraits, or military-simulation severity.
Don't use glass, neon edge glows, purple gradients, soft SaaS cards, or fake terminal jargon.
Don't activate gameplay prefabs, networking components, colliders, or authoritative scripts for menu decoration.
Don't let continuous animation overlap controls or become required feedback.
